note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 65; docs/CURRICULUM.md, experiment 14) on data/benches/standardise.json: sodium hydroxide standardised against KHP. KHP + NaOH -> KNaP + H2O, one to one: the base's concentration = m(KHP) / (204.22 g/mol x V(base)).
title: Experiment: standardising a base

report.label: the base's concentration
report.why: c = m / (M V): the balance's reading of the KHP over 204.22 g/mol, in the base the burette ran in (its two readings' difference). The label said about 0.1 M: sodium hydroxide takes up water and carbon dioxide from the air, so its solution is made roughly and standardised. The balance reads within 0.2 mg, the burette within 0.05 mL, and the last drop past the end point is the titration's own error.

steps.title: The flask on the balance
steps.text: Click the titration flask to pick it up, then click the balance. Then right-click the balance and click "tare".
steps.why: A primary standard is weighed: KHP is pure, dry, not hygroscopic, and heavy for the one hydrogen it gives up (204.22 g/mol), so half a gram of it is weighed to 0.04 %.

checks.text: the flask tared on the balance

steps.title: About half a gram of KHP
steps.text: Pick up the KHP, then right-click the flask. Type 0.5, then click "tip 0.5 g of the solid".

steps.title: What the balance says
steps.text: Right-click the balance and click "+ mass": the KHP you took, to 0.1 mg.

steps.title: Water, stirred
steps.text: Pick up the water bottle, right-click the flask, type 50 and click "pour". Then right-click the flask, click "stir", and click 60x on the clock.
steps.why: The water's volume does not matter: the moles of KHP are what the base meets.

steps.title: Three drops of phenolphthalein
steps.text: Pick up the phenolphthalein, right-click the flask, type 0.15 and click "pour".
steps.why: Phenolphthalein is colourless below pH 8 and pink above 9: past the end point the first drop of base turns the whole flask pink. The end point of a weak acid's titration with a strong base is near pH 9, in its range.

steps.title: Fill the burette
steps.text: Pick up the sodium hydroxide, right-click the burette, type 55 and click "pour".

steps.title: Its first reading
steps.text: Right-click the burette and click "+ mL": it reads down from its zero line.

steps.title: The burette over the flask
steps.text: Pick up the burette and click the flask: its tip stands in the flask's neck.

steps.title: Most of it, fast
steps.text: Right-click the burette and drag its tap to about 30 %.
steps.why: Half a gram of KHP takes about 25 mL of a 0.1 M base: the first 18 mL can run in fast.

steps.title: To 18 mL
steps.text: Watch the burette until it reads 18 mL.

steps.title: Then drop by drop
steps.text: Drag the burette's tap nearly shut, to about 4 %.
steps.why: Near the end point a drop is what matters: the last drop past it is the titration's error.

steps.title: The first lasting pink
steps.text: Watch the flask until it turns pink and stays pink.

steps.title: Shut it, and read it
steps.text: Drag the burette's tap shut, then right-click the burette and click "+ mL". The base run in is the two readings' difference.
